subject: ARA
label: Grade 04
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 04 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Seasons and weather
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Seasons and weather', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe the weather and seasons. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Seasons and weather' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe the weather and seasons, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: في الصيف الجو حار وفي الشتاء الجو بارد. أذهب إلى الشاطئ في الصيف. (In summer it is hot, in winter cold. I go to the beach in summer.) Method: Model run for 'Seasons and weather'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe the weather and seasons: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name the four seasons. الرَّبِيعُ [spring], الصَّيْفُ [summer], الْخَرِيفُ [autumn], الشِّتَاءُ [winter]. Say them in order and point to a calendar. Notice that الرَّبِيعُ, الصَّيْفُ and الشِّتَاءُ start with a sun letter, so the l of الْ is silent.

Step 2, Learn weather words. الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ [The weather is hot]. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ [cold]. الْجَوُّ مُعْتَدِلٌ [mild]. الْجَوُّ مُمْطِرٌ [rainy]. الْجَوُّ مُشْمِسٌ [sunny]. Ask: كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ [How is the weather today?]

Step 3, Describe each season. فِي الصَّيْفِ يَكُونُ الْجَوُّ حَارًّا. [In summer the weather is hot.] فِي الشِّتَاءِ تَهْطِلُ الْأَمْطَارُ. [In winter rain falls.] فِي الرَّبِيعِ تُزْهِرُ الْأَزْهَارُ. [In spring flowers bloom.] فِي الْخَرِيفِ تَسْقُطُ أَوْرَاقُ الْأَشْجَارِ. [In autumn the leaves fall.]

Step 4, Short dialogue. سَلْمَى: كَيْفَ الْجَوُّ الْيَوْمَ؟ [How is the weather today?] عُمَرُ: الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ وَمُمْطِرٌ. [The weather is cold and rainy.] سَلْمَى: أَيُّ فَصْلٍ تُحِبُّ؟ [Which season do you like?] عُمَرُ: أُحِبُّ الرَّبِيعَ. [I like spring.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says الْجَوُّ حَارَّةٌ. Correction: الْجَوُّ is masculine, so say الْجَوُّ حَارٌّ. But for a feminine noun use the feminine form: الشَّمْسُ حَارَّةٌ [The sun is hot]. Match the adjective to its noun.

Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences about your favourite season and its weather. Model answer: أُحِبُّ الشِّتَاءَ لِأَنَّ الْأَمْطَارَ تَهْطِلُ. الْجَوُّ بَارِدٌ وَأَلْبَسُ مِعْطَفًا. [I like winter because rain falls. The weather is cold and I wear a coat.]

modules.title: Gardens and animals
modules.outcome: describe a garden and its animals
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Gardens and animals', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: describe a garden and its animals. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Gardens and animals' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe a garden and its animals, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: في الحديقة زهور وشجرة وعصفور. العصفور يطير. (In the garden are flowers, a tree and a bird. The bird flies.) Method: Model run for 'Gardens and animals'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Describe a garden and its animals: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Name things in a garden. حَدِيقَةٌ [garden], شَجَرَةٌ [tree], وَرْدَةٌ [rose], عُشْبٌ [grass], فَرَاشَةٌ [butterfly], نَحْلَةٌ [bee], عُصْفُورٌ [sparrow], أَرْنَبٌ [rabbit]. Label a picture with these words.

Step 2, Describe with adjectives that agree. شَجَرَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ [a big tree], وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ [a beautiful rose], أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرٌ [a small rabbit]. The adjective copies the gender of the noun and adds ـَةٌ for a feminine noun.

Step 3, Say what is in the garden. فِي الْحَدِيقَةِ شَجَرَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ. [In the garden there is a big tree.] تَقِفُ عَلَيْهَا عَصَافِيرُ. [Sparrows stand on it.] الْفَرَاشَةُ تَطِيرُ بَيْنَ الْأَزْهَارِ. [The butterfly flies among the flowers.]

Step 4, Say what animals do. الْأَرْنَبُ يَأْكُلُ الْجَزَرَ. [The rabbit eats carrots.] النَّحْلَةُ تَجْمَعُ الرَّحِيقَ. [The bee collects nectar.] Ask: مَاذَا تَفْعَلُ النَّحْلَةُ؟ [What does the bee do?] تَجْمَعُ الرَّحِيقَ. [It collects nectar.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلٌ. Correction: وَرْدَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ, because وَرْدَةٌ is feminine. Another says أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. Correction: أَرْنَبٌ صَغِيرٌ, because أَرْنَبٌ is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: describe a garden with a white rabbit and a red rose. Model answer: فِي حَدِيقَتِي أَرْنَبٌ أَبْيَضُ وَوَرْدَةٌ حَمْرَاءُ. الْأَرْنَبُ يَأْكُلُ الْعُشْبَ. [In my garden there is a white rabbit and a red rose. The rabbit eats grass.]

modules.title: Conversation practice
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Conversation practice', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: ask and answer questions. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Conversation practice' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: ask and answer questions, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: — السلام عليكم، هل أستطيع التحدث إلى أحمد؟ — وعليكم السلام، لحظة من فضلك. (Hello, may I speak to Ahmed? One moment please.) Method: Model run for 'Conversation practice'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Ask and answer questions: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn question words. مَا [what], مَنْ [who], أَيْنَ [where], مَتَى [when], كَمْ [how many], لِمَاذَا [why], كَيْفَ [how]. Say each with a pointing hand. Remember مَنْ asks about people and مَا about things.

Step 2, Ask personal questions to a boy. مَا اسْمُكَ؟ [What is your name?] كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ [How old are you?] أَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ [Where do you live?] مَاذَا تُحِبُّ؟ [What do you like?] To a girl the endings change: مَا اسْمُكِ؟ كَمْ عُمْرُكِ؟

Step 3, Answer in a full sentence. اسْمِي سَلْمَى. [My name is Salma.] عُمْرِي تِسْعُ سَنَوَاتٍ. [I am nine years old.] أَسْكُنُ فِي مَدِينَةٍ كَبِيرَةٍ. [I live in a big city.] أُحِبُّ الْقِرَاءَةَ. [I like reading.]

Step 4, Practise a conversation. عَلِيٌّ: مَرْحَبًا، مَا اسْمُكِ؟ [Hello, what is your name?] سَلْمَى: اسْمِي سَلْمَى، وَمَا اسْمُكَ؟ [My name is Salma, and yours?] عَلِيٌّ: اسْمِي عَلِيٌّ. أَيْنَ تَسْكُنِينَ؟ [My name is Ali. Where do you live?] سَلْمَى: أَسْكُنُ فِي الْحَيِّ الْقَدِيمِ. [I live in the old quarter.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child asks مَنْ اسْمُكَ؟ Correction: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ because a name is a thing, not a person. Another answers the question كَمْ عُمْرُكَ؟ with أَنَا مِنْ مِصْرَ; reply with the age, عُمْرِي عَشْرُ سَنَوَاتٍ [I am ten years old].

Step 6, Your turn: ask a new classmate two questions and answer two yourself. Model answer: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ وَأَيْنَ تَسْكُنُ؟ اسْمِي مَرْيَمُ، وَأَسْكُنُ بِجَانِبِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ. [What is your name? And where do you live? My name is Maryam, and I live next to the school.]

One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
